# Corpus texts

Static excerpts used as the sample corpus for the benchmarks and the accuracy bounds. They are checked in as-is and are not regenerated by any script.

The corpus is meant to represent what people actually measure with tokenx: chat logs, API responses, documentation pages and prose, across scripts. Registers are chosen deliberately – contemporary simplified Chinese rather than traditional or classical, because those merge differently and would move the figure without representing anyone's traffic.

Subject matter moves the estimate by more than the script does, which is why the CJK entries are one topic across three languages rather than one page translated three ways: a translated page carries the source language's code blocks and product names into every version, and those price identically in all three.

Each prose file was cleaned once: source boilerplate and markup removed, hard-wrapped lines rejoined into whole paragraphs, one paragraph per line separated by a blank line. Latin-script wraps were rejoined with a space, CJK wraps with nothing. The Markdown and JSON files are kept verbatim, because the raw form is what tooling feeds through an estimator.

The benchmark also measures `src/index.ts`, `src/segments.ts` and `src/types.ts` as a source-code sample, so no file is checked in for that row.

`../holdout/` holds a separate set of texts that no ratio was ever fitted against – see `test/holdout.test.ts`. They carry their own licences:
